title: error
description: One error in the errors list of an answer. Every app uses this one format, so a reader handles any app's errors the same way (ADR-S03).

apiVersion.description: The form the error is in, as <org>/<app>/<family>/v<n>. An error carries its own version like everything an app answers, so it can be read even on its own (ADR-S15).

kind.description: Always Error, so an error is told apart from every other kind, even outside an answer (ADR-S15).

code.description: A short word for what went wrong, such as unsupported_contract. A program decides by the code, never by the message, so the message can be reworded without breaking a reader.

message.description: What went wrong, in plain words for a person. A program reads code instead, so this text may be reworded.

at.description: The place the error points to, so a person or a tool goes straight to what needs fixing. Left out when the error is about no one place.

file.description: The file the error is in, so a person can open it.

kind.description: The kind of the resource the error is about. An id is unique only within a kind, so kind and id together name one resource.

id.description: The id of the resource the error is about; read together with kind.

field.description: The field inside the resource that is wrong, as a path such as spec.board.display.layout, so a person finds the exact line to fix.

supported.description: For unsupported_contract: the contract versions the app answers. A reader that asked for a version the app cannot give picks one from this list that it also speaks and asks again (ADR-S03, ADR-S06).
